chapter: Early recordings and arrival in New York
title: Hearing Ella and John Kirby in Pittsburgh in 1932
summary: She remembers promoting a dance near Homestead, Pennsylvania, where Ella's band played with John Kirby on bass.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: And possibly she did rather better before. I mean, there's a beautiful song she made with Teddy Wilson in 1936 which I love. It's called "All My Life."
I heard they were. So far, (inaudible) listen to recordings, you know, nine times out of ten everything that that particular person makes, they're going to like.

But you need one song. I remember hearing one of Ella's old records, Rhythm and Romance, which I loved. In fact, all of us here have done quite a few recordings before I even thought about coming to New York.
In fact, in Pittsburgh -- I'm actually from Homestead, Pennsylvania which is a little small town outside of Pittsburgh -- and I happened to belong to a club called the "Prosperity Club." And we had

a dance -- we promoted a dance -- and for some reason or other, the band -- the Chick Webb Bank -- had been playing in Pittsburgh at one of the theaters. And it was their last night and they were closing. I don't know how we happened to get them, except for the fact that we had a very dynamic president of the club who could get just about anything she wanted.
Do you remember what year this was?

It had to be 1932. In fact, I have an autographed book with Ella's autograph in it, and she doesn't even know if she signed it. But I was waiting tables during the affair. And all of a sudden I heard this voice and I knew it was Ella Fitzgerald. I didn't wait tables the rest of the night. I went and sat right in front of the bad. And I think this was one of the first tours that Ella was out on. This was right after she first got started. And it was Chick Webb's band.

And incidentally, John Kirby was playing the bass with the band that night. And Clift Jackson was here on the piano, because I got both of their autographs.
I didn't know one musician from the other at that time. We had a lot of bands coming through.
Okay. Well I've seen reference to that story in the line notes, the album, John Kirby on the bass, on Columbia.
I think it was 1932 because I have the -- my autograph book. Well this is later. This date is wrong. It should be 1932.
You really can't remember those dates sometimes.
